Ruminant.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ruminant.question: The _____ was Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.
Ruminant.fact: Ruminants are herbivorous grazing or browsing artiodactyls belonging to the suborder Ruminantia that are able to acquire nutrients from plant-based food by fermenting it in a specialized stomach prior to digestion, principally through microbial actions. The word ruminant comes from the Latin rūminārī, "to ruminate", from rūmen, the first stomach.

Ruminant.subject: Environment & Ecology

Ruminant.fact: Until the beginning of the 21st century, it was understood that the family Moschidae (musk deer) was sister to Cervidae. However, a 2003 phylogenetic study by Alexandre Hassanin (of National Museum of Natural History, France) and colleagues, based on mitochondrial and nuclear analyses, revealed that Moschidae and Bovidae form a clade sister to Cervidae.

Ruminant.subject: Environment & Ecology
Ruminant.question: Monogastric herbivores, such as rhinoceroses, horses, guinea pigs, and _____, are not ruminants, as they have a simple single-chambered stomach
Ruminant.fact: Monogastric herbivores, such as rhinoceroses, horses, guinea pigs, and rabbits, are not ruminants, as they have a simple single-chambered stomach. In smaller hindgut fermenters of the order Lagomorpha (rabbits, hares, and pikas), and Caviomorph rodents (Guinea pigs, capybaras, etc.), material from the cecum is formed into cecotropes, passed through the large intestine, expelled and subsequently reingested to absorb nutrients in the cecotropes.

In total, the area of Sundaland is approximately 1,800,000 km2.  The area of exposed land in Sundaland has fluctuated considerably during the past recent 2 million years; the modern land area is approximately half of its maximum extent.  The western and southern borders of Sundaland are clearly marked by the deeper waters of the Sunda Trench – some of the deepest in the world – and the Indian Ocean.  The eastern boundary of Sundaland is the Wallace Line, identified by Alfred Russel Wallace as the eastern boundary of the range of Asia's land mammal fauna, and thus the boundary of the Indomalayan and Australasian realms. Sundaland.subject: Environment & Ecology
Sundaland.question: The fish is now found in the _____ on the island of Borneo, and in the Musi and Batanghari rivers in Sumatra
Sundaland.fact: As a result, the modern islands of Sundaland are home to many Asian mammals including elephants, monkeys, apes, tigers, tapirs, and rhinoceros.  The flooding of Sundaland separated species that had once shared the same environment.  One example is the river threadfin (Polydactylus macrophthalmus, Bleeker 1858), which once thrived in a river system now called "North Sunda River" or "Molengraaff river".  The fish is now found in the Kapuas River on the island of Borneo, and in the Musi and Batanghari rivers in Sumatra.  Selective pressure (in some cases resulting in extinction) has operated differently on each of the islands of Sundaland, and as a consequence, a different assemblage of mammals is found on each island.  However, the current species assemblage on each island is not simply a subset of a universal Sundaland or Asian fauna, as the species that inhabited Sundaland before flooding did not all have ranges encompassing the entire Sunda Shelf.  Island area and number of terrestrial mammal species are related, with the largest islands of Sundaland (Borneo and Sumatra) having the highest diversity

Sundaland.subject: Environment & Ecology
Sundaland.question: Snow was found much lower than at present (approximately 1,000 meters lower) and there is evidence that glaciers existed on Borneo and _____ around 10,000 years before present
Sundaland.fact: The presence of fossil coral reefs dating to the late Miocene and early Pliocene suggests that, as the Indian monsoon grew more intense, seasonality increased in some portions of Sundaland during these epochs.  Palynological evidence from Sumatra suggests that temperatures were cooler during the late Pleistocene; mean annual temperatures at high elevation sites may have been as much as 5 °C cooler than present.  Most recent research agrees that Indo-Pacific sea surface temperatures were at most 2-3 °C lower during the Last Glacial Maximum.  Snow was found much lower than at present (approximately 1,000 meters lower) and there is evidence that glaciers existed on Borneo and Sumatra around 10,000 years before present.  However, debate continues on how precipitation regimes changed throughout the Quaternary.  Some authors argue that rainfall decreased with the area of ocean available for evaporation as sea levels fell with ice sheet expansion.  Others posit that changes in precipitation have been minimal and an increase in land area in the Sunda Shelf alone (due to lowered sea level) is not enough to decrease precipitation in the region

Tetrapod.fact: Since the early 20th century, several families of tetrapodomorph fishes have been proposed as the nearest relatives of tetrapods, among them the rhizodonts (notably Sauripterus), the osteolepidids, the tristichopterids (notably Eusthenopteron), and more recently the elpistostegalians (also called Panderichthyida) notably the genus Tiktaalik. A notable feature of Tiktaalik is the absence of bones covering the gills.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: 2) _____ represents a case of parallel evolution
Tetrapod.fact: Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this date discrepancy: 1) The nearest common ancestor of tetrapods and Tiktaalik dates to the Early Devonian. By this hypothesis, the lineage is the closest to tetrapods, but Tiktaalik itself was a late-surviving relic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The adult tetrapods had an estimated length of _____ (8 feet), and lived in a lagoon with an average depth of 1–2 m, although it is not known at what depth the underwater tracks were made
Tetrapod.fact: The adult tetrapods had an estimated length of 2.5 m (8 feet), and lived in a lagoon with an average depth of 1–2 m, although it is not known at what depth the underwater tracks were made.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The oldest partial fossils of tetrapods date from the Frasnian beginning ≈_____ mya
Tetrapod.fact: The oldest partial fossils of tetrapods date from the Frasnian beginning ≈380 mya.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: These include _____ and Obruchevichthys
Tetrapod.fact: These include Elginerpeton and Obruchevichthys.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The publication in _____ of Tutusius umlambo and Umzantsia amazana from high latitude Gondwana setting indicate that the tetrapods enjoyed a global distribution by the end of the Devonian and even ext
Tetrapod.fact: The publication in 2018 of Tutusius umlambo and Umzantsia amazana from high latitude Gondwana setting indicate that the tetrapods enjoyed a global distribution by the end of the Devonian and even extended into the high latitudes.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: This gap, which was initially _____ years, but has been gradually reduced over time, currently occupies much of the 13.9-million year Tournaisian, the first stage of the Carboniferous period
Tetrapod.fact: This gap, which was initially 30 million years, but has been gradually reduced over time, currently occupies much of the 13.9-million year Tournaisian, the first stage of the Carboniferous period.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: When stem-tetrapods reappear in the fossil record in early Carboniferous deposits, some _____ years later, the adult forms of some are somewhat adapted to a terrestrial existence
Tetrapod.fact: When stem-tetrapods reappear in the fossil record in early Carboniferous deposits, some 10 million years later, the adult forms of some are somewhat adapted to a terrestrial existence.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The first amniotes are known from the early part of the _____
Tetrapod.fact: The first amniotes are known from the early part of the Late Carboniferous.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Amphibians and amniotes were affected by the Carboniferous rainforest collapse (CRC), an extinction event that occurred around _____ years ago
Tetrapod.fact: Amphibians and amniotes were affected by the Carboniferous rainforest collapse (CRC), an extinction event that occurred around 307 million years ago.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Sauropsid diversity was more subdued during the _____, but they did begin to fracture into several lineages ancestral to modern reptiles
Tetrapod.fact: The latter were the most important and successful Permian land animals, establishing complex terrestrial ecosystems of predators and prey while acquiring various adaptations retained by their modern descendants, the mammals. Sauropsid diversity was more subdued during the Permian, but they did begin to fracture into several lineages ancestral to modern reptiles.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Some temnospondyls, seymouriamorphs, and diadectomorphs also successfully filled terrestrial niches in the earlier part of the _____
Tetrapod.fact: The latter were the most important and successful Permian land animals, establishing complex terrestrial ecosystems of predators and prey while acquiring various adaptations retained by their modern descendants, the mammals. Sauropsid diversity was more subdued during the Permian, but they did begin to fracture into several lineages ancestral to modern reptiles.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The end of the _____ saw a major turnover in fauna during the Permian–Triassic extinction event
Tetrapod.fact: Some temnospondyls, seymouriamorphs, and diadectomorphs also successfully filled terrestrial niches in the earlier part of the Permian. Non-amniote tetrapods declined in the later part of the Permian.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Some of the new _____ reptiles would not survive into the Jurassic, but others would flourish during the Jurassic
Tetrapod.fact: The end of the Permian saw a major turnover in fauna during the Permian–Triassic extinction event. Some of the new Triassic reptiles would not survive into the Jurassic, but others would flourish during the Jurassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Lizards, turtles, dinosaurs, pterosaurs, crocodylomorphs, and plesiosaurs were particular beneficiaries of the _____-Jurassic transition
Tetrapod.fact: Some of the new Triassic reptiles would not survive into the Jurassic, but others would flourish during the Jurassic. Lizards, turtles, dinosaurs, pterosaurs, crocodylomorphs, and plesiosaurs were particular beneficiaries of the Triassic-Jurassic transition.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Birds, a particular subset of theropod dinosaurs capable of flight via feathered wings, evolved in the _____
Tetrapod.fact: Birds, a particular subset of theropod dinosaurs capable of flight via feathered wings, evolved in the Late Jurassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: In the _____, snakes developed from lizards, rhynchocephalians (tuataras and kin) declined, and modern birds and crocodilians started to establish themselves
Tetrapod.fact: In the Cretaceous, snakes developed from lizards, rhynchocephalians (tuataras and kin) declined, and modern birds and crocodilians started to establish themselves.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Temnospondyls briefly recovered in the _____, spawning the large aquatic stereospondyls and the small terrestrial lissamphibians (the earliest frogs, salamanders, and caecilians)
Tetrapod.fact: Temnospondyls briefly recovered in the Triassic, spawning the large aquatic stereospondyls and the small terrestrial lissamphibians (the earliest frogs, salamanders, and caecilians). However, stereospondyl diversity would crash at the end of the Triassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: However, stereospondyl diversity would crash at the end of the _____
Tetrapod.fact: Temnospondyls briefly recovered in the Triassic, spawning the large aquatic stereospondyls and the small terrestrial lissamphibians (the earliest frogs, salamanders, and caecilians). However, stereospondyl diversity would crash at the end of the Triassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: By the _____, the only surviving amphibians were lissamphibians
Tetrapod.fact: By the Late Cretaceous, the only surviving amphibians were lissamphibians.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Many groups of synapsids, such as anomodonts and therocephalians, that once comprised the dominant terrestrial fauna of the _____, also became extinct during the Triassic
Tetrapod.fact: Many groups of synapsids, such as anomodonts and therocephalians, that once comprised the dominant terrestrial fauna of the Permian, also became extinct during the Triassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: During the _____, one synapsid group (Cynodontia) gave rise to the modern mammals, which survived through the rest of the Mesozoic to later diversify during the Cenozoic
Tetrapod.fact: During the Jurassic, one synapsid group (Cynodontia) gave rise to the modern mammals, which survived through the rest of the Mesozoic to later diversify during the Cenozoic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Birds survived and diversified during the _____, similar to mammals
Tetrapod.fact: During the Jurassic, one synapsid group (Cynodontia) gave rise to the modern mammals, which survived through the rest of the Mesozoic to later diversify during the Cenozoic. Birds survived and diversified during the Cenozoic, similar to mammals.

Tetrapod.fact: One of them, a group of semiaquatic reptiles called the Choristodera, became extinct 11 million years ago for unclear reasons.

Tetrapod.fact: There are two variants, one developed by Carroll, the other by Anderson.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Besides the opercular series, _____ also lost the throat-covering bones (gular series)
Tetrapod.fact: In Acanthostega, a basal tetrapod, the gill-covering bones have disappeared, although the underlying gill arches are still present. Besides the opercular series, Acanthostega also lost the throat-covering bones (gular series).

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Acanthostega had the same arrangement as _____, and thus no neck joint
Tetrapod.fact: In tetrapodomorph fishes such as Eusthenopteron, no such neck joint existed. Acanthostega had the same arrangement as Eusthenopteron, and thus no neck joint.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: The ancestors of the ray-finned fishes (_____) evolved their fins in a different direction
Tetrapod.fact: The ancestors of the ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii) evolved their fins in a different direction.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: This has been confirmed by fossilized footprints found in _____ rocks
Tetrapod.fact: This has been confirmed by fossilized footprints found in Carboniferous rocks.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Others have suggesting a mode of feeding comparable to that of the _____ giant salamander, which uses both suction feeding and direct biting to eat small crustaceans and fish
Tetrapod.fact: Others have suggesting a mode of feeding comparable to that of the Japanese giant salamander, which uses both suction feeding and direct biting to eat small crustaceans and fish.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Some aquatic temnospondyls retained internal gills at least into the early _____
Tetrapod.fact: Some aquatic temnospondyls retained internal gills at least into the early Jurassic.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Evidence of clear fish-like internal gills is present in _____
Tetrapod.fact: Evidence of clear fish-like internal gills is present in Archegosaurus.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: About fifty million years later (late _____), in mammals, the columella was reduced even further to become the stapes
Tetrapod.fact: Only in the early Triassic, about a hundred million years after they conquered land, did the tympanic middle ear evolve (independently) in all the tetrapod lineages. About fifty million years later (late Triassic), in mammals, the columella was reduced even further to become the stapes.

Tetrapod.subject: Environment & Ecology
Tetrapod.question: Amphibians and amniotes were affected by the _____ rainforest collapse (CRC), an extinction event that occurred around 307 million years ago
Tetrapod.fact: The first amniotes are known from the early part of the Late Carboniferous. All basal amniotes had a small body size, like many of their contemporaries, though some Carboniferous tetrapods evolved into large crocodile-like predators, informally called "labyrinthodonts".
